By Mike Allen · Aug 21, 2026

🥳 Happy Friday! Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 545 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Trump promises cheaper beef
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios

President Trump said today that he would temporarily increase tariff-free beef imports and that he had secured a commitment to sell the meat at 25% below current market prices, Axios' Nathan Bomey reports.

  • A global cattle shortage has driven up the cost for red meat, making burgers and steaks more expensive.

🤳 Trump said on Truth Social that he had "concluded a deal to substantially lower the price of ground beef for working American families."

  • He added, "We have a commitment that this beef will be sold at 25 percent below current market prices."
  • "As we work to rebuild this herd and help our ranchers, for the next 90 days, the United States will allow up to 300,000 metric tons of product for ground beef to be imported with no out of quota tariff."

🤔 Reality check: Trump didn't specify who made the commitment to sell the beef at a lower price.

  • A White House official said the commitment came from foreign beef exporters, and that the 25% discount would be passed along to U.S. consumers.

Go deeper.
 
 
2. 🏀 NBA merry-go-round keeps on spinning
 
Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios

Marc Lore has agreed to sell his controlling stake in the NBA's Minnesota Timberwolves and the WNBA's Minnesota Lynx to billionaire investor Marc Stad at a $4.5 billion enterprise value, Axios' Dan Primack reports.

  • That comes just a week after Mark Walter agreed to sell the Los Angeles Lakers to Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger for $12.5 billion.

🐺 Lore — a serial entrepreneur and former Walmart exec — gained control of the Timberwolves last summer, after a protracted legal process.

  • Lore's partner on the deal, ex-MLB player Alex Rodriguez, will remain a part of club ownership.

📆 Behind the scenes: The deal has been in process for several months, per a source familiar — which means it wasn't a reaction to the Lakers sale.

  • Go deeper.
 
 

A MESSAGE FROM GOLDMAN SACHS

AI’s impact on the labor market
 
 

Rapidly improving AI capabilities and growing corporate adoption have raised concerns about a potential AI "job apocalypse."

Although the types of jobs available may continue to shift, the likelihood of large-scale job losses remains unlikely.

Read the report from Goldman Sachs Research.

 
 
3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Argentina's Leandro Paredes gets violent with Spain's Gavi after last month's FIFA World Cup Final. Photo: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images
  1. ⚽️ FIFA has banned three Argentina players, including a 10-match suspension for midfielder Leandro Paredes, for striking their Spanish opponents after losing the World Cup final. Go deeper.
  2. 📚 The FTC is being urged to investigate AI companies for buying, scanning and destroying books to train their models, per a letter first shared with Axios' Ashley Gold. Go deeper.
  3. 📺 A super PAC linked to Sen. Ted Cruz is launching a more than $1.7 million ad campaign to boost Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton, Axios' Stef W. Kight has learned. Go deeper.
  4. 🛒 SNAP food aid enrollment dropped by more than 13% in a 12-month span. That's a far steeper decline than the government estimated as work requirements and other parts of President Trump's "big beautiful bill" take effect. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 🐿️ 1 fun thing: Fat Marmot Week
 
A marmot named 9 sits outside her den on Aug. 6 in Gothic, Colo. Photo: Brittany Peterson/AP

Fat Marmot Week is helping scientists drum up donations for their research into the furry ground squirrels living high in the Colorado mountains.

  • The riff on Fat Bear Week starts Monday, and comes as federal funding cuts jeopardize the researchers' work.

🔬 The local marmot study, run by UCLA researchers about 20 miles south of Aspen, has been ongoing since 1962 — making it one of the world's longest-running studies of individual mammals.

  • The researchers need to bank three years of funding — over $200,000 — to keep working next summer.

How electric vehicles and AI are driving M&A in rare earths
 
 

Rising demand for electric vehicles and AI infrastructure is reshaping the mining and processing of critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and rare earth elements.

The impact: dealmaking is accelerating as companies race to secure supply chains and meet growing demand.
